items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Two of my close friends, Neal Hefti, and Johnny Mandel even more than Neal because I sort of grew up with Johnny, he was my roommate on the Buddy Rich band

ctx.x: Yeah, you were playing some great arrangements, huh?

Shorty Rogers, Ralph Burns, Johnny Mandel, you name it. Neal Hefti. You go down the list of guys. Two of my close friends, Neal Hefti, and Johnny Mandel even more than Neal because I sort of grew up with Johnny, he was my roommate on the Buddy Rich band, they make so much money on — not so much on the songs that they wrote that are popular like for example “The Shadow of Your Smile,” “Emily,” “A Time for Love,” that Johnny Mandel wrote and Neal wrote “Cute” and “L’il Darling” and all these things — they wrote…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: But if Johnny Mandel was alive or Al Cohn or Manny Albam, these great arrangers, they would tell you they learned arranging from what Tiny was doing.

ctx.x: Everybody in the world has one. So, and you could relate to all, and all kids who play in the streets could relate to my stories, you know. So and I was lucky to have a great childhood. I grew up with Tiny Kahn, see Tiny Kahn is when I was from 6 years old until I went in the Army at 19 or 18, until I got with Woody Herman’s band really. We were together day and night. And if you can, people who know these names can imagine what we looked like at 15 years old, we looked like Peter Lorre and Sydney Greenstreet…

items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I still argue with Terry Gibbs that he should have had in the Dream Band, he should have had four rhythm.

ctx.x: ‘Cause the kind of music we played, I think Woody’s band really should have had a guitar. There’s a lot of guys that are very hardheaded about three-piece rhythm sections though, that I still argue with Terry Gibbs that he should have had in the Dream Band, he should have had four rhythm. He said, “Nah, it was a bebop band, I like three rhythm.” If you had the right guitar player it wouldn’t matter, if you're playing that kind of big band jazz music.
If you had a Barry Galbraith.
